name: Technological University Dublin
overview:
ADDITIONAL PROGRAMME SPECIFICS


  • Non European students are not allowed to apply to TU Dublin
  • Good level in math required


TECHNOLOGICAL UNIVERSITY DUBLIN


Technological University Dublin (TU) was founded in 1992, but had already existed under another name and structure since 1887.

Nearly 22,000 students attend TU Dublin, which offers four distinct fields of study through four different colleges:

  • College of Arts & Tourism
  • College of Business
  • College of Engineering & Built Environment
  • College of Sciences & Health


Each college has been recognized as a center of excellence in its field.


Campus and Location


Each department has its own premises, all dispersed within Dublin city center.


The building for Tech 4 students is located in the city center, just a 5-minute walk from lively areas filled with:

  • Bars
  • Restaurants
  • Shopping, etc.


Travel Advisory

administrative:
Application Dossier


Once the IAFF office has sent your nomination, the partner university will contact you directly by email to start your application.


All required documents will need to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline

(see the EMEA Teams channel for each application deadline).

If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet — please be patient.


To be completed with your Epitech bachelor campus administration during the registration period for Tech4 (usually in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


Visa

  • For European students: A valid passport or national ID card is sufficient to travel within Europe (exception: UK)
  • For non-European students or students with non-European citizenship: Please check the immigration office of the host country for visa process and fees
Students in France can consult: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/


Insurance


For European Students


  • The European Health Insurance Card (CEAM) is nominative and individual
  • It certifies your rights to Health Insurance in Europe
  • Obtain it by logging into your Ameli account at least two months before departure
  • It is free of charge and will be sent within two weeks (also available as a downloadable version)
More information: https://www.ameli.fr/assure/droits-demarches/europe-international/protection-sociale-etranger/etudes-etranger


For Non-European Students


  • You must register for private health insurance to cover your full stay
  • Please consult your parents, bank, or private insurance provider based on the desired coverage


Travel Safety


French citizens should register with the Ariane platform (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) to receive alerts regarding safety risks such as terrorist attacks, tsunamis, earthquakes: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html


Campus Life & Accommodation


Technological University Dublin does not have its own residence, but can help you find housing in external student residences.

  • Accommodation assistance: http://www.dit.ie/campuslife/studentsupport/accommodation/
  • Other recommended housing platforms:
  • http://www.daft.ie/
  • http://campus.ie/surviving-college/student-accommodation
  • http://www.rent.ie/
  • www.collegecribs.ie


Tip: Favor telephone contact — it often takes 2 to 3 weeks to secure accommodations and requires persistence


General Advice

  • Start your housing search well in advance
  • Rates are variable
  • For economic and practical reasons, consider colocation (shared housing)


Arrival & Transportation


If you complete the "Student Arrival Form" at least one week before arriving, the International Higher Education Students Department can offer airport pickup to your accommodation:

  • https://www.tudublin.ie/study/international-students/pre-departure-and-arrival-2021-22/
  • (See section "Before you Travel")


Payment & Security

  • If renting from a private individual, you’ll likely be asked to pay:
  • First month’s rent
  • One month’s deposit
  • In cash → plan with your bank accordingly
Beware of scams!
Housing scams are present in all countries — stay cautious and verify offers.
accomodation:
Technological University Dublin does not have its own residence, but can help you find accommodations in other residences. We invite you to visit the following link to find out more : http://www.dit.ie/campuslife/studentsupport/accommodation/ .


You can also find accommodations on the following sites: http://www.daft.ie/, http://campus.ie/surviving-college/student-accommodation , www.collegecribs.ie and http://www.rent.ie/. We advise you to favor contact by telephone. It takes two to three weeks to find accommodations. It takes a lot of persistence!


It can be very difficult to find accommodation on your own in Dublin. You should begin your search well in advance of your arrival.


Rates are variable. For practical and economic reasons, consider colocation.


Please note: If you fill out the following form "Student Arrival Form" at least one week prior to our arrival, the International Higher Education Students Department offers a pick up service from the airport to your accommodation:

https://www.tudublin.ie/study/international-students/pre-departure-and-arrival-2021-22/ section "Before you Travel".


Please note: If you rent accommodation from a private individual, you will certainly be asked to pay the first month's rent and a month's deposit in cash. You should plan this with your bank.

courses:
Academic Requirements


For both programs, you will need to earn 40 local credits for the full academic year, equivalent to 8 modules.

If you wish, you may take more than 8 modules during the year.


Programs Offered at TU Dublin – Aungier Street Campus


1.CPD in IT Management


Seats available: 10 maximum


This program focuses on the business of IT and is offered by the Business and Computing Department.

Most courses are worth 5 credits, so you must take a minimum of 4 courses per semester:

  • 2 compulsory modules per semester
  • Minimum 2 optional modules
A good level in mathematics is recommended.


Semester 1 Modules:

  • Strategic Management
  • Mobile Application Development
  • Project Management
  • Business Modelling
  • Future of Work
  • Performance Management
  • Communication and Professional Skills
  • Organisational Change


Semester 2 Modules:

  • Strategic Management
  • Strategic Information Systems
  • Software Quality Assurance
  • Business Decision Making
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Communication and Teamwork
  • Human Resource Management
  • Quality Management and Performance Improvement


2.CPD in Data Analytics


Seats available: 10 maximum

This new CPD program includes modules in database, business management, and data science.


A good level in mathematics (especially statistics) is required.


You will learn about software, tools, and techniques used in data analytics, including how to manage them effectively.


Semester 1 Modules:

  • Management Science 1
  • Time Series Analysis
  • Project Management
  • Simulation for Business Analytics
  • NoSQL Database Management
  • Statistical Programming
  • Business Intelligence
  • Information Retrieval and Processing
  • Applied Predictive Analytics


Semester 2 Modules:

  • Management Science 2
  • Statistical Forecasting
  • Simulation for Business Analytics
  • Business Decision Making
  • Machine Learning Techniques for Data Analysis
  • Software Framework for Large Data Sets
  • Big Data Concepts
  • Dynamic Programming Languages


Additional Information

  • Some modules are mixed between Irish and international students
  • Class schedules may be spread out over the week, depending on the professor and student availability
  • You may also obtain a Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Diploma


Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of exclusion from the university
  • The course list is provided for informational purposes only and may change from year to year
  • If a course is unavailable on arrival, EPITECH cannot be held responsible


EIP

Any Tech4 abroad involves an EIP!

Use any free slots in your schedule to make progress on your EIP.
cost:
Estimated Budget


Roundtrip Airfare


  • From Europe:
  • Approximately €40 with only a small cabin accessory
  • Add €40 per checked-in luggage with a low-cost company
  • Minimum of €200 for Air France-like companies
  • From Réunion Island:
  • At least €1200
  • (You need to travel to Paris first, then go to Ireland)


Insurance

  • European "Améli" insurance card (free)
  • Note: If you want to be reimbursed, it will be necessary to make the requests to your French insurer after the services


Accommodation

  • Between €700 and €900 per month per student for a shared flat (excluding charges)
  • Minimum of €1000 per month per student for an ensuite bedroom in student accommodation
  • Minimum of €1500 per month for a private flat

Please note: It is very difficult to find accommodation in Dublin.


Sports Center

  • University complex: Free, but there are schedules to be respected according to the sport
  • Gym membership: Between €30 and €80, depending on the gym


Food

  • €100–150 per month minimum for Lidl-like grocery stores
  • Plan a little more if you like to go out and go to restaurants or pubs
  • (Pint of Guinness starts at €5)


Transport

  • Taxi: €30–40 from the airport to Dublin city center
  • Bus: Student Leap Card allows you to pay €1 per trip (instead of €2.60)
  • Airport shuttle bus: Approximately €7


You can easily go around in Dublin on foot, as the city is not very big.


Important Notes

  • Prices are indicative and may vary
  • The cost of living (accommodation, food, and transport) is higher than in France
